text: in January 2024 a solar panel manufacturer named First Solar
quietly finalized a real estate purchase in Wood County Ohio
the purchase price was $33 million
for that money
they didn't just get 200 acres of prime industrial farmland
they got a 1 dot 2 million square foot
unfinished monolith of structural steel
poured concrete and vacant assembly bay
thirty three million sounds like real money
until you look at the company that poured the concrete
less than three years earlier
this exact parcel of dirt
was announced as the crown jewel of American consumer tech
it had a name the Peloton Output Park
a 400 million dollar mega factory
engineered to stamp out 1.5 million connected exercise bikes
every single year employing 2,000 American workers
$400 million committed 33 million recovered
a 70+ percent loss on invested capital
wiped out before a single stationary bike ever rolled off the line
most people remember the peloton story as a comedy of errors
they remember the viral 2019 Christmas commercial
where an anxious wife filmed a video diary about her exercise bike
they remember that episode of the sex and the city reboot
where Mr Big suffered a fatal heart attack on a peloton bike
plus tanking the company's stock 11% overnight
and they remember Ryan Reynolds
frantically producing a parody commercial 48 hours later
with the actor to prove he was still alive
only for the campaign to implode four days later
when the actor was hit with serious sexual assault allegations
it was chaotic it was tabloid ready and it made for great memes
but here is the reality Mr Big didn't kill Peloton
Ryan Reynolds didn't kill peloton
and the viral Christmas ad didn't erase
$50 billion of enterprise value
what destroyed peloton was a lethal accounting mirage
corporate executives convinced Wall Street and themselves
that a capital heavy manufacturer of heavy consumer
metal was actually an asset light Silicon Valley software platform
and by the time they realized that
every single bike rolling out of their warehouses
was actively bleeding hundreds of dollars of cash
they had already spent billions
building an industrial empire for customers that did not exist
this is the forensic autopsy of how $50 billion vanished into thin air
to understand how the machine broke
you have to look at the man who built it
John Foley Foley was not an industrial supply chain engineer
he was an e commerce executive
who spent years pitching venture capitalists on a simple
intoxicating premise
he didn't want to sell you a metal exercise bike
he wanted to sell you an ongoing lifestyle subscription
when peloton went public on the NASDAQ in September 2019
institutional investors didn't value it
like Nordic Track or Nautilus
those traditional fitness companies traded at boring
cyclical multiples maybe one or two times their annual revenue
peloton claimed to be fundamentally different
in their investor pitch the exercise bike was just a Trojan horse
you buy the hardware once for twenty two hundred dollars
and then you pay 39 dollars every single month
forever to stream live workouts from charismatic celebrity instructors
on paper the unit economics were gorgeous
in software customer acquisition cost
or cack is the money you spend on marketing to win one paying customer
usually that marketing expense burns cash up front
but throughout fiscal 2020
Peloton had a secret weapon
because affluent early
adopters were happy to pay over $2,000 for the bike
peloton made roughly 43% gross profit on the physical hardware alone
that meant every time someone bought a bike
peloton cleared roughly $900 of gross cash
before the customer even turned on the screen
that $900 completely paid for the Facebook ads
the showroom leases in upscale shopping malls
and the marketing campaigns
in Wall Street terms their customer acquisition was virtually free
and once that customer was plugged in
they stayed monthly churn was under 1%
Wall Street looked at those numbers and lost its mind
investors said this isn't a hardware business
this is Netflix on a bike
um and then came March 2020
Covid 19 shuttered every commercial gym in North America and Europe
overnight millions of professionals with disposable income
found themselves trapped in their living rooms
terrified and bored the demand didn't just climb
it detonated
monthly workouts per subscriber surged past 24
delivery backlog stretched from two weeks to eight weeks
then to 10 weeks customer service phone lines were overwhelmed
in December 2020 Peloton's market valuation passed $50 billion
John Foley was a billionaire
the instructors were signing seven figure talent contracts
but right here at the absolute peak of the frenzy
executive leadership made the foundational mistake
that would seal their fate
they confused a temporary crisis driven pull forward of demand
with a permanent structural expansion of their market
they looked at customers
technically ordering bikes during a global quarantine
and assumed that this was the new normal
baseline of human civilization
and instead of staying asset light
and letting customers wait out the pandemic
peloton decided to build an industrial empire in logistics
there is a famous concept known as the bullwhip effect
imagine you are holding a whip
if you flick your wrist just two inches
the tip of the whip 50 feet away cracks violently
through the air across 20 feet
in industrial manufacturing
customer demand is the risk
if consumer demand temporarily jumps 10%
retailers panic and increase their orders by 20%
wholesalers see that 20% spike and order 40% more from factories
and by the time the signal reaches the raw material suppliers
orders have amplified into a massive distorted wave
Peloton's executive suite took the bullwhip
and swung it with both hands
in December 2020 Peloton paid $420 million in pure cash to buy Precor
a commercial fitness equipment manufacturer
purely to acquire their factories in North Carolina and
Washington
next came the freight panic
port congestion in Long Beach
and Los Angeles
was delaying shipments from their Asian contract manufacturers
so what did peloton do they charted entire Boeing 777 cargo freighters
to fly thousands of 70 pound steel bikes across the Pacific Ocean
spending up to $100 million on expedited air freight
just to get bikes into living rooms two weeks faster
and then in May 2021 came the big bet
the 400 million dollar peloton output park in Ohio
2,000 workers 1.2 million square feet
Foley declared that peloton would control its own industrial destiny
for decades to come
structural steel began rising from the Ohio dirt in late 2021
and then the world reopened
vaccines rolled out people walked out of their apartments
commercial gyms unlocked their doors
and the demand for 22 dollar stationary bikes didn't just normalize
it fell off a cliff
every wealthy household that wanted a peloton already had one
sitting in their spare bedroom
increasingly serving as an expensive clothes rack
the backlog evaporated overnight
but the container ships
full of raw parts were still crossing the ocean the pre core fact
was still producing metal and the concrete in Ohio was still drying
the bullwhip snapped back and the crack shattered their balance sheet
look closely at Peloton's form 10K
filing for the fiscal year ended June 30th, 2022
this is where the mathematical horror story is buried
to clear mountains of bikes piling up in third party warehouses
management started slashing prices
from 22 hundred dollars down to 14 hundred dollars
meanwhile ocean container rates had spiked fivefold
storage fees were compounding daily
and air freight amortization was hitting the Ledger
and then the arithmetic inverted
in fiscal 2020 every bike delivered generated $927 in gross profit
by fiscal 2022 every single bike delivered generated a loss of $196
before paying a single cent for marketing
salaries or software development
previously hardware gross profit paid for customer acquisition
now acquiring a customer burned cash on the marketing
burned cash on the delivery
and burned cash on the hardware itself
the machine was devouring its own capital
but bad financial math wasn't their only problem
an engineering catastrophe was unfolding
peloton had launched a luxury motor
this treadmill the tread plus
priced at 40 three hundred dollars
unlike traditional treadmills that use a flat
continuous belt sliding across a deck with a low ground clearance
the tread plus used 59 individual rubber coated
interlocking aluminum slats powered by a heavy industrial motor
crucially the elevated rear roller sat 6 to 8 inches above the floor
without a physical safety guard
or an automatic emergency shut off threshold
if a small pet
a yoga ball or a child was pulled underneath the moving slats
the powerful motor did not stop
it dragged them beneath the belt in early
2021 horrific incident reports
began piling up on the public
docket of the US Consumer Product Safety Commission
dozens of children were pulled under the machine
suffering severe abrasions
broken bones and blunt force trauma
in March 2021 a six year old child died
on April 17th, 2021 the CPSC issued an extraordinary public warning
urging consumers with children and pets to stop using the Tread Plus
immediately what did Peloton's executive leadership do to John Foley
publicly called the government's safety warning outrageous
inaccurate and misleading
refusing to recall the machine
and insisting it was perfectly safe
if consumers followed instructions
it was a staggering display of corporate hubris
for 18 days
management dug in while outrage exploded across national media
finally on May 5
Foley was forced to issue a humiliating public apology
and recall all 125,000 Tread Plus machines
taking an immediate 365 million dollar write down
eighteen months later
federal regulators would extract their pound of flesh
a 19 million dollar civil penalty
for failing to immediately report known hazards
the government's consent order revealed that peloton had
received more than 150 reports of people
pets and objects being pulled under the machine
before ever contacting regulators
even worse the audit found that peloton
had knowingly delivered 38 recalled Tread Plus units to customers
after the recall was declared
the brand's premium Halo
the trust of affluent suburban parents was broken beyond repair
why hadn't the board of directors stopped the bleeding months earlier
because of a corporate voting mode when peloton went public
it issued two class
of stock
Class a shares owned by regular retail investors and retirement funds
had one vote per share class B shares
held almost exclusively by John Foley and his founding inner circle
carried 20 votes per share
with less than 20% of the actual economic ownership
Foley and his team controlled over 80% of the voting power
they were untouchable Foley could ignore safety warnings
spend hundreds of millions on charter cargo planes
and pour concrete in Ohio
and public shareholders could do nothing
all while executives cashed out over $100 million in stock sales
near the market top the wall finally broke on January 24th, 2022
activist investment fund
Blackwell's Capital published a scathing presentation
publicly demanding that the board fire John Foley immediately
and explore a sale of the company
Blackwell's laid out the catastrophic forensic record
selling general and administrative expenses up hundreds of percent
bloated corporate payrolls
and hundreds of millions committed to an unneeded Ohio mega
factory while the core hardware business bled cash
Foley tried to hold on but institutional lenders
and Class a shareholders delivered an ultimatum
on February 8th, 2022 John Foley was removed as CEO
in his place the board installed Barry McCarthy
the former chief financial officer of Netflix and Spotify
McCarthy was an institutional surgeon
he had zero emotional attachment to Foley's dream of an integrated
industrial kingdom within 48 hours
McCarthy swung the axe construction on the 400 million dollar
Ohio mega factory was permanently stopped
2,800 jobs were eliminated in a single day
proprietary delivery vans were shut down
replaced with third party delivery contractors
proprietary factories were abandoned
all hardware manufacturing was surrendered back to overseas
contract manufacturers
when the final accounting books closed on fiscal 2022
the damage was staggering
a net loss of $2.8 billion in including $415 million
inventory write downs for bikes and raw parts
were literally scrapped
McCarthy spent two years ruthlessly cutting costs
shrinking headcount from over 9,000 employees down to under 3,000
and slashing warehouse leases but by 20
24 Peloton faced a new structural nightmare
their own past success
millions of pristine
barely used peloton bikes were sitting in basements
hundreds of thousands of owners were listing them on Facebook
Marketplace and Craigslist for $400
less than a quarter of the retail price
every time someone bought a secondhand bike on Craigslist
Peloton made zero dollars in hardware revenue and the Mark
for new bikes dried up completely in August 2024
in an act of pure desperation
peloton instituted a mandatory $95
used activation fee
forcing second hand buyers to pay a toll just to register a bike
they already legally owned
on May 2 2024
exhausted and out of levers to pull
Barry McCarthy resigned on January 1st, 2025
Peter Stern
the former co founder of Apple Fitness Plus took over as CEO
he inherits a business valued not at $50 billion
but at roughly two billion
a modest niche subscription utility
servicing a loyal but stagnant base of dedicated fitness enthusiasts
it is the oldest lesson in corporate finance
you cannot value a factory like an algorithm
software scales with a line of code
physical manufacturing scales with steel
concrete freight containers and human hands
when a once in a century crisis pulls tomorrow's demand into today
the discipline lies in knowing that the storm will pass
and if you spend billions
building an empire for a world that only exists inside a quarantine
the reckoning is inevitable
just ask the solar company
that bought a 400 million dollar Monument to hubris
in Wood County Ohio
